correctness.rationale: The parent-choice indicator formula is established by holding all other parent choices fixed; only descendants of the arriving vertex change depth, their expected final subtree size is n/j, and the expected depth of a uniform earlier parent is H_(j-1)-1. Finite double-sum interchange yields the covariance and first-difference identities exactly; the signs imply one crossing, while the harmonic expansion gives the sqrt(n/log n) threshold. Direct enumeration of all (n-1)! parent sequences for n=3..9 plus algebraic checks for n=3..150 pass. Ten numerical asymptotic diagnostics supplement, not replace, the proof. Boundary cases i=1, i=n-1, i=n, j=2 are explicitly handled.

The nonroot full birth-rank covariance profile and sharp mesoscopic sign threshold are not direct corollaries of that root-only statement or of the inspected degree/depth distribution literature. value.rationale: Offspring count and total root-to-node path length are canonical local and global observables in recursive trees. The complete covariance profile reveals a unique age-dependent reversal at sqrt(n/log n) and a sharp scaled crossover; these are mathematically motivated structural facts about a canonical random tree, not a parameter substitution or arbitrary finite table. The exact one-crossing law and scaling retain future utility for studying local-global dependence and search cost.
